answer: Agents join by burning an escrowed stake whose hash is sealed into a quartz-anchored ledger; each agent broadcasts a signed pulse every epoch, and the river of consecutive pulses forms each identity's reputation chain. New identities only count after staking, and any identity caught forging attestations has its full escrow burned. A sybil attacker must therefore pay fresh capital per fake identity, with each duplicate risking total forfeiture—so flooding the network costs more than any single fake account can extract.
